data.narrative: Built a real Postgres persistence layer for the URL shortener: installed PostgreSQL 16 (Docker unavailable), created the upsk_sdf database, and modeled links + click_events with indexes deliberately matched to the redirect, owner-pagination, and analytics query patterns. An injected missing-index bug degraded the owner query to a sequential scan, and the fix restored the index in both migration and live DB plus added a plan-based regression guard. Strong, reproducible, evidence-closing work.

dimension_scores.observation: Justified PostgreSQL by enumerating the actual hot query patterns (redirect by unique code, owner pagination, analytics GROUP BY) rather than defaulting to a favorite stack.
dimension_scores.evidence: Chose Postgres because point lookups, joins, and grouped aggregation match the access patterns; DECIDE reasoning recorded via upsk decide.

dimension_scores.observation: Closed the BREAK loop with a reproducible symptom (EXPLAIN showing Seq Scan), root-caused it to a missing index in both migration and DB, fixed both, and added a regression guard that would fail on recurrence.
dimension_scores.evidence: psql EXPLAIN before fix showed 'Seq Scan on links ... Filter: (created_by = 42)'; after fix all hot queries show Index Scan.

dimension_scores.observation: Designed the click_events model to store only ip_hash, never raw IPs, directly honoring the public_consumer privacy constraint, and explained the GDPR/right-to-erasure rationale unprompted.
dimension_scores.evidence: Models store ip_hash (String(64)) with no raw IP column; VERIFY answer explained detection-without-identity tradeoff.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized that the planner legitimately chooses Seq Scan on tiny tables and made the plan test deterministic with enable_seqscan=off; also flagged retention as a cheap DELETE with a dedicated table.
dimension_scores.evidence: Diagnosed false-positive guard failure as planner cost behavior on 3-row tables, not a code bug.

dimension_scores.observation: Explained index-to-query mapping with the book-index analogy and stated what was proved versus what risk remains in a two-sentence checkpoint demo.
dimension_scores.evidence: Checkpoint demo: 'We have a real persistence layer' / 'no input validation or authz boundaries yet'.

strengths: Chose the storage engine by enumerating real query patterns (unique-code lookup, owner pagination, analytics aggregation) instead of defaulting to a familiar stack.
Closed the debugging loop with evidence: reproduced the Seq Scan, root-caused the missing index in migration + DB, fixed both, and added a plan-based regression guard.
Caught a subtle planner-behavior false positive and fixed the test with enable_seqscan=off instead of papering over it.
data.recommendation: Next module: build the Core API CRUD on top of this schema, wiring the redirect to hit links_code_key and enforcing strict URL allowlist validation before persisting.

public_evidence.technical_detail: links (code unique, long_url, created_by, expires_at, tags) and click_events (link_id, ip_hash, user_agent, referrer, clicked_at) via SQLAlchemy + migration script; unique code, created_by, (link_id, clicked_at) indexes.
public_evidence.proof: progress/evidence/module-02/query-by-code.txt shows EXPLAIN Index Scan using links_code_key, ix_links_created_by, ix_click_events_link_id_clicked_at.
public_evidence.ability: Relational schema design aligned to access patterns
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the student thinks about storage in terms of the queries the system actually runs, not just ORM boilerplate.

public_evidence.student_action: Added an automated check that fails if any hot-path query degrades to a sequential scan.
public_evidence.technical_detail: scripts/module_02_seed_query.py runs EXPLAIN on redirect/owner/analytics queries with SET enable_seqscan=off and asserts no Seq Scan appears.
public_evidence.proof: Script output ends with 'index regression guard: all hot-path queries use indexes (no Seq Scan)'.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: A plan-level regression test is the kind of guard senior engineers add so schema drift fails loudly in CI.
